text:
This was my first time using this clinic with my government health insurance, and I don't intend to return.

- When I went in, the dentist told me to rinse with antiseptic mouthwash. I only saw plain water, so I asked the assistant, "Is this it?" The assistant said, "Yes, that's it." So I rinsed with plain water. After spitting it out, the dentist told me not to rinse with plain water again. I looked again, and there was still only plain water. I asked again, and I still couldn't see the antiseptic mouthwash I was supposed to use.
- When I went in to have the painful tooth examined, the dentist tapped the tooth quite hard without any prior warning. I was very shocked. Luckily, the pain wasn't too bad at that point, because if it had been still painful, the dentist's tapping would have been very painful. The dentist said that tooth needed root canal treatment and that we would decide later.
- The dentist then asked if I wanted them to fill the remaining teeth today. The filling cost would be calculated per side. The dentist showed me teeth with small cavities, both visible and invisible. So I told the dentist that I would only have one side filled today so I could use my government health insurance. The dentist said, "Okay, I'll fill this tooth." I agreed because the dentist pointed out that tooth only had a small cavity on one side. After a while, the dentist said... The dentist also filled the side of the tooth, so the customer had to pay extra for that side as well. At the time, I couldn't say anything because it was already done and the instruments were in my mouth. Even though I had stated my request from the beginning and the dentist had chosen that tooth myself, when I checked later, I couldn't see any change to the side that the dentist said was filled.

Other things I encountered included:
- While I was filling out the information, the staff were chatting and complaining about other customers.
- I arrived half an hour before my appointment but still had to wait almost an hour, even though no one else was waiting.
- The pricing information was inconsistent. The price at the counter didn't match the price the dentist quoted, making it difficult to make a decision.
- During the procedure, my mouth was full of water, and I had to keep swallowing.
- While waiting to pay, I asked the staff for more information about the root canal treatment price, but they just looked at each other and smiled without answering. I'm not sure what they were trying to convey. Also, when I said I wanted to postpone my next appointment, I asked for the page name to contact them later, but they wouldn't give it to me. After waiting a while, the staff kept urging me to make an appointment, emphasizing that I needed treatment. I had to ask again for the information before they finally provided it.

One thing I found impressive was that the customer was wearing shorts. While I was having my teeth done, the staff covered my lower body with a blanket.

The doctor is good, and every visit has been excellent. However,
this time, the communication and service need improvement. We went in for wisdom tooth extraction.
Issue 1: We asked the doctor if they could issue a 7-day medical certificate.
Doctor: Oh no, that's not possible (loudly).
We: But I drink alcohol every day.
Doctor: No, you can't.
We: I drink alcohol every day for work.
Doctor: At most, you can get a 3-day certificate.
We: So, does that mean I can drink alcohol on the 4th day?
Doctor: I don't recommend it. I suggest you abstain for now.
Issue 2: The price of the wisdom tooth extraction.
Before this, we checked the prices for tooth extraction, fillings, and wisdom tooth extraction both at the counter and over the phone. The clinic stated that wisdom tooth extraction cost 1,800-3,000 THB. However, on the day of the service, the bill came to 3,500 THB, and the doctor who performed the extraction didn't inform us of the price before or after the procedure. Normally, every time we come to this clinic, the doctor informs us of the price of the service beforehand. So, how many instances of miscommunication were there this time? Both the front counter staff and the doctor.
